text:
Maya: alert — multiple probes show west-us-2 control plane and node heartbeats missing. Grafana: ~98% of instance heartbeats stale, LB 502/504 spike. Tagging oncall.
InfraBot: Automated alert: region-westus2-heartbeat-failure at 2026-03-14T09:12:03Z — runbook link: https://confluence.redwood/infra/runbooks/region-failover
Maya: kubectl to cluster API times out, `connection refused` from control plane endpoints.
Sam: I'm on it — running quick health checks and tcpdump. Will try hitting master IPs directly.
Oliver: Starting preemptive capacity in east-us-1 and eu-west-1. Recommend traffic migration to east-us-1 for latency parity.
Maya: Note: 4 reserved customers have pinned capacity in west-us-2. Need to confirm data residency constraints before moving them.
Leah: @Maya list customer IDs and SLA tiers, I'll page CSMs and legal if needed.
Sam: quick check output:
```bash
$ for ip in $(cat westus2-control-ips); do curl -sS http://$ip:6443/healthz || echo "down $ip"; done
down 10.40.1.12
down 10.40.1.13
down 10.40.2.7
```
Maya: Network telemetry shows repeated BGP flaps to our west-us-2 upstream provider — NetOps alerted.
NetOps: upstream provider reported partial peering outage affecting transit to west-us-2, investigating root cause.
Oliver: Proposing staged traffic shift: 30% -> east-us-1 immediately, monitor errors, then full cutover if control plane stays unreachable.
Leah: Runbook check: if control plane unreachable >10m, initiate failover. We're at ~14 minutes. Recommend failover now.
Maya: Agreed. Actions: 1) set routing policy to prefer east-us-1, 2) scale east-us-1 GPU pools to absorb burst, 3) notify affected customers & CSMs, 4) keep west-us-2 marked as degraded in console.
Sam: Executing infra commands now:
```text
infractl route update --from west-us-2 --to east-us-1 --weight 0 --dry-run=false
infractl pool scale --region east-us-1 --pool gpu-prod-v2 --replicas 6
```
InfraBot: Route update accepted, job 983412 queued. Scale job started: job 983413.
Oliver: Heads up: scaling GPU pools rapidly will increase spend — rough estimate +$12k/day if maintained. Recommend enabling autoscale with a max cap.
Maya: Set autoscale max and enable prefix cache to reduce token cost on warmups. Also enable graceful draining on west-us-2 to avoid throttling running jobs.
Leah: CS notified. CSM-Bot: paging messages sent to the 4 affected tenant owners.
NetOps: Provider says partial transit recovered at 09:44 UTC but control plane calls remain intermittent. Suggest keep failover active and monitor for stable 30m window.
Sam: Control plane API responded briefly at 09:44 but became unstable again. We've collected packet captures and API logs and uploaded to the incident folder: https://s3.redwood/incident/1767501234/pcap.tar.gz
Oliver: I'll lead the post-incident next steps: timeline, packet captures, BGP updates, routing decision rationale, cost impact.
Maya: Marking incident SEV2. Moving to incident bridge for deeper investigation — bridge invite sent.
Leah: Thanks all — documenting decisions and actions in the incident doc. Owner: Oliver + Sam.
Maya: Closing the Slack triage loop, continuing work on the bridge. :white_check_mark:
